title: The hover effect of st.date_input varies depending on the value of min_value
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary When the value of `min_value` in `st.date_input` falls within the current month, no hover effect is applied when hovering over the dates in the calendar. ``` from datetime import datetime, timedelta import streamlit as st specified_date_input = st.date_input( label="test", key="test", value=None, max_value="today", min_value=(datetime.now() - timedelta(days=7)).date(), disabled=False, ) ``` However, when the value of `min_value` extends into the previous month, a hover effect is applied. ``` from datetime import datetime, timedelta import streamlit as st specified_date_input = st.date_input( label="test", key="test", value=None, max_value="today", min_value=(datetime.now() - timedelta(days=31)).date(), disabled=False, ) ``` Is this behavior a bug? Is it possible to standardize the hover effect? ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python ``` ### Steps To Reproduce _No response_ ### Expected Behavior _No response_ ### Current Behavior _No response_ ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: - Python version: - Operating System: - Browser: ### Additional Information _No response_

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15653)

This is a visual bug in `st.date_input`'s calendar popover where the per-day hover ring indicator is inconsistent depending on whether the `min_value` falls within the currently visible month. When `min_value` is within the current month (so the visible month contains a mix of disabled and enabled dates), hovering an enabled date does not show the hover ring; when `min_value` lies in a previous month (so all dates in the visible month are enabled), the hover ring renders normally.

Looking at `frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/DateInput/DateInput.tsx` (the `Day` overrides around lines 345–395), the hover ring is driven by BaseWeb's `$isHighlighted` state on the `::after` pseudo-element:

```tsx
"::after": {
  borderColor: $isHighlighted
    ? colors.primary
    : colors.transparent,
},
```

The likely root cause is upstream in BaseWeb's Datepicker: when `minDate` falls inside the visible month, BaseWeb appears to suppress/skip the `$isHighlighted` state on hover for the focusable days (probably tied to how it manages keyboard focus/highlight initialization when disabled days are present in the same month). Background coloring via `::before` (`$isHovered`) still works, but the ring on `::after` (`$isHighlighted`) does not. This may need to be either worked around in our overrides (e.g. fall back to `$isHovered` for the ring border) or reported/fixed upstream in BaseWeb.

### Related Issues

- [#10929](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10929) (closed) — Previous hover-color bug in `st.date_input` where hovered dates inside a selected range didn't change color. Closely related (same widget, same hover-style area) and the fix touched the exact `Day` overrides where this new regression appears.
- [#9667](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9667) — `st.date_input` greys out years that fall within the valid `min_value`/`max_value` range. Related: another visual inconsistency in the calendar UI tied to `min_value`/`max_value` (also flagged as `upstream` BaseWeb behavior).
- [#12802](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12802) — Hover border color inconsistency in `st.segmented_control`. Not the same widget, but the same class of bug: per-cell hover styling that renders inconsistently depending on neighboring state.
